source_citation: SKY130A PDK voltage-level definitions (Phase 0 verified primitives); multi-valued logic noise-margin theory from Hirasuna (1999) and Pécot et al.; radix-economy from Thomas K. Moon (2005), 'Fundamentals of Digital Logic'

binary_radix2_1p8v.note: Standard binary CMOS logic levels at 1.8 V nominal VDD

quaternary_q4_1p8v_ldo.note: Phase 0 verified Q4 voltage map on SKY130 1.8 V LDO rail; 4 distinct levels with 0.6 V spacing

quaternary_q4_1p65v.name: Q4 Quaternary — 1.65 V profile (alternative)
quaternary_q4_1p65v.note: Lower-margin alternative profile for tighter power budgets

verified_sky130a_q4_primitives.function: quaternary threshold detector — maps analogue input to nearest Q4 digit
quaternary inverter — Q3→Q0, Q2→Q1, Q1→Q2, Q0→Q3
4:1 quaternary multiplexer — selects one of 4 Q4 inputs by 2-digit selector
quaternary half adder — Q4 sum (mod 4) + Q4 carry

equations: radix_economy: E(r) = r / log₂(r) — the cost-per-digit ratio; minimized at r = e ≈ 2.718, making radix-3 theoretically most economical
noise_margin_NMH = V_OH(min) − V_IH(max); noise_margin_NML = V_IL(max) − V_OL(max)
Q4 levels: L_k = k · VDD / 3 for k = 0..3 with VDD = 1.8 V
binary_levels: L_k = k · VDD for k = 0..1
ternary_levels: L_k = k · VDD / 2 for k = 0..2
theoretical_noise_margin_bounds: NM ≥ VDD / (2·(r − 1)) for r uniformly spaced levels on a railed logic family
Q4 inversion: Q3 → Q0, Q2 → Q1, Q1 → Q2, Q0 → Q3 (equivalent to 3 − Q in mod-4)
Q4 half adder: S = (A + B) mod 4, C = ⌊(A + B) / 4⌋

valid_operating_envelope.note: SKY130 commercial operating range; logic-level voltages scale proportionally with VDD

failure_thresholds.note: SKY130 core SOA ceiling; the Q4 voltage map (max 1.8 V) is safely below this ceiling
